annotation.title_clean: Drones and new systems of warfare – the EU's need to adapt to be fit for today's security challenges
annotation.title_en: Drones and new systems of warfare – the EU's need to adapt to be fit for today's security challenges
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union (C series)
annotation.summary_en: European Parliament own-initiative resolution of 22 January 2026 urging the EU to adapt to drone warfare. It calls for counter-drone capabilities, an EU Drones Package and binding regulation of military and civilian drones, faster certification, sovereign supply chains, SME funding and Ukraine cooperation, and requires human-in-the-loop control over lethal autonomous drones under international humanitarian law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Calls on the Commission to propose an EU Drones Package, including a regulation on civilian and military drone use
Calls for a binding EU regulatory framework for military drone operations, covering rules of engagement, certification and ethical safeguards
Requires autonomous drones to be governed by international humanitarian law and a human-in-the-loop principle for lethal force
Supports a 'drone wall' and EU-wide counter-UAS interoperability through open modular standards in EDF-funded programmes
Proposes EU-origin component criteria, a Drone Sovereignty Index, and stockpiles to cut dependency on China
